oml:flow.oml:name: pdll._classifier.PairwiseDifferenceClassifier
oml:flow.oml:description:
Pairwise Difference Classifier (PDC), a scikit-learn meta-estimator.
PDC turns a (multiclass) classification task into a binary one: the base estimator learns whether two points belong to the *same* class from the pair ``[x_a, x_b, x_a - x_b]``. To classify a new point, PDC compares it with every training point (the *anchors*), whose labels are known, and turns the predicted similarities into class probabilities. Tree ensembles such as ExtraTrees or RandomForest typically gain accuracy from this, especially on small tabular datasets.
Read more in Belaid, Rabus & Hüllermeier, *Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification*, Discovery Science 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.20031 (``pdll.__citation__`` holds the BibTeX).

oml:parameter.oml:name: class_weight
oml:parameter.oml:description: Weights of the classes, applied as sample weights (see ``fit``). ``"balanced"`` gives every class the same total weight; on imbalanced data this counters PDL's tendency to under-predict minority classes (in our benchmark: up to +0.05 macro-F1, never worse). Needs a base estimator whose ``fit`` accepts ``sample_weight``. ``None`` (default) weighs every row equally, as in the paper

oml:parameter.oml:name: estimator
oml:parameter.oml:description:
Binary classifier used on the pairs. It is cloned, never modified. ``None`` means ``ExtraTreesClassifier(class_weight="balanced", n_jobs=-1)``. Prefer tree-based models and ``class_weight="balanced"``: only about 1/n_classes of the pairs are "same class"
use_prior : {"auto", True, False}, default="auto" How similarities become probabilities. ``True``: the prior-based posterior of the paper, averaged over anchors. ``False``: the mean similarity to each class, normalised ``"auto"``: ``True`` if some class has fewer than 5 training rows, else ``False``

oml:parameter.oml:name: max_anchors
oml:parameter.oml:description:
Prediction compares each point with every anchor, so its cost grows with the number of anchors If the training set is larger, a class-stratified random subset of ``max_anchors`` rows is used as anchors. ``None`` uses every training row
max_pairs : "auto", int or None, default="auto" The base estimator is trained on n² pairs. If that exceeds ``max_pairs``, a uniform random subset of ``max_pairs`` pairs is used. ``"auto"`` means 100,000 pairs (every pair up to 316 training rows), fewer for very wide data so the pair matrix stays below 0.5 GB. ``None`` uses every pair, as in the paper; time and memory then grow with n²

oml:parameter.oml:name: random_state
oml:parameter.oml:description: Seeds the pair and anchor subsampling, and the base estimator if its own ``random_state`` is None.
